role: Block device imaging: read, write, verify, hash, format. Agentic successor to dd; human successor to balenaEtcher/Rufus/Ventoy.

capabilities.name: list
capabilities.description: Enumerate available block devices with size, type, mount state, and removability.

capabilities.name: info
capabilities.description: Detail one device or image file: format detection, size, partitions, and safety classification.

capabilities.name: ontology
capabilities.description: Emit the machine-readable capability ontology for agent discovery.

capabilities.name: checksum
capabilities.description: Compute MD5, SHA-256, SHA-512, BLAKE3, or CRC32 over a file or a whole block device.

capabilities.name: verify
capabilities.description: Check that a device or file matches a source image or expected hash.

capabilities.name: write
capabilities.description: Write a disk image to a target block device, decompressing gz/bz2/xz/zstd/zip in flight. Overwrites the target entirely.

capabilities.name: format
capabilities.description: Format a block device with a filesystem. Erases all existing data.

note: Grants follow abt's own ontology, which declares destructive and requires_elevation per capability: write and format carry both flags and are the only two that require a grant. Budgets follow cost rather than danger, which is why they do not line up with grants. checksum and verify need no authority but read an entire device, so their cost scales with the target rather than the request; format is the reverse — a single privileged decision whose danger is that it was unauthorised, not that it was repeated. INCOMPLETE BY CONSTRUCTION: abt exposes 49 commands and its ontology declares 7, so this manifest covers 7. The 42 undeclared include destructive operations — erase, clone, restore, backup, diff, persist, multiboot, customize — and an agent must not read this manifest, or abt's ontology, as the full surface. Closing that gap is a change to abt's ontology, not to this file.
